speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the timing of your symptoms. Did the right leg weakness and unsteady gait start suddenly or gradually, and are the forgetfulness and paranoia present all the time or only when you are confused?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the subacute onset of right leg weakness combined with cognitive decline, I need to rule out a structural lesion in the brainstem or spinal cord. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast and MRI Cervical Spine. While we await those results, have you noticed any changes in bowel or bladder control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary CNS Lymphoma. Given the subacute onset of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, cognitive decline, paranoia, and the presence of lymphadenopathy, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of an infiltrative neoplasm affecting the brain and systemic lymphatic system. The MRI results pending will likely show an enhancing mass lesion consistent with this diagnosis.
